market_sizing.target_buyer: Owner / managing director of a 3D printing service bureau (often technical founder, 2–25 employees). In larger bureaus (>15 staff) ops manager / production lead drives selection with founder sign-off.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Estimated 150–300 dedicated 3D printing / additive manufacturing service bureaus in AU. The AU 3D printing market is ~USD 672m (2025) growing at ~17% CAGR. Major players include CAC Works, 3D Forge, E-Jet 3D Printing, Parallax Studio, Infinity 3D Printing, plus listed companies (Titomic, Conflux, Amaero, Aurora Labs, Spee3D). Long tail of single-owner Form-print / FDM bureaus. Reachable SMB target: ~150–250 bureaus today; growing.
market_sizing.business_count_global: Global SMB 3D-print service bureau count: ~5,000–10,000. US: ~1,500–2,500; Europe: ~2,000–3,000; UK: ~300–500; CA: ~200–400. Plus university/maker-space labs (~10,000+) that are adjacent but lower-willingness-to-pay. Voxelmatters/All3DP directories list a few hundred named bureaus globally but the long tail is much larger.
market_sizing.typical_size: 2–20 employees, AUD 300k–5m revenue. Sweet spot 5–12 staff with AUD 800k–3m revenue.

pricing_reality.incumbent_pricing: MakerOS: free tier (10 employees, 30GB), Pro USD 239/mo (20 employees, 300GB, API). 3DPrinterOS: contact-sales pricing, education-heavy. AMFG: enterprise pricing typically USD 500–2,000/mo, MES-grade. DigiFabster: subscription, instant-quoting focus, mid hundreds USD/mo. Phasio: cloud workflow + portal, monthly subscription. Slicer/CAM software (PrusaSlicer, Cura, Bambu Studio) free. Most small bureaus pay USD 0–250/mo today and run Excel + Stripe + Trello.
pricing_reality.willingness_to_pay: AUD 100–400/mo entry, AUD 500–1,000/mo for mid bureaus with multiple printers and instant-quote portals. Bureaus are tech-savvy (slicer-fluent) and price-sensitive — they expect SaaS UX and won't tolerate enterprise pricing for entry. AU-adjusted blended ARPU: AUD 200–350/mo.
pricing_reality.sales_motion: Predominantly self-serve with light inside sales. Bureaus discover tools via Reddit, LinkedIn, All3DP, slicer forums, and YouTube. Free trial → paid is the standard motion. Enterprise/managed-MES sales possible for AMFG-scale deals but rare in AU.
pricing_reality.realistic_arpu_au: AUD 200–350/mo blended. Entry AUD 99/mo (1–2 printers, basic quote), mid AUD 349/mo (instant quote portal, workflow), high AUD 799+/mo (MES, queue across printers, AS9100/ISO 13485 traceability).
pricing_reality.expansion_revenue_potential: Moderate-to-strong. (1) Per-printer pricing scales naturally as bureau adds machines. (2) Embedded payments — bureaus invoice AUD 200k–3m/yr; 1–2% take-rate is meaningful. (3) Marketplace lead-flow (bring jobs to bureaus) — significant but competitive with Xometry/Hubs. (4) Material / consumables resale (resin, filament, powder). (5) AI quote / DFM analysis. (6) Certification add-on for medical (ISO 13485) / aerospace (AS9100). 2–3× expansion plausible but ceiling lower than for finishing/fab because bureaus are smaller.

competitive_landscape.incumbents: 1) **MakerOS** (US, founded ~2017) — business mgmt for 3D print bureaus; pivoted to free entry tier 2021, paid USD 239/mo. Limited recent traction signals. 2) **3DPrinterOS** (US/UK, ~2014) — print queue + management, strong in education/enterprise, less SMB-friendly. 3) **AMFG** (UK, ~2017) — MES for additive, enterprise-leaning, USD 500–2,000+/mo. 4) **DigiFabster** (US, 2016) — instant quoting + e-commerce, subscription, popular with quoting-focused bureaus. 5) **Phasio** (Singapore, 2021) — customer portal + order mgmt for SME manufacturers, partnered with 3D Industrie in DACH. 6) **AutoQuote3D** — instant-quoting tool, narrower. 7) **3DPBOSS** — smaller niche. 8) Marketplaces (not direct competitors but eat into work): Xometry (USD 687m FY2025 revenue), Protolabs/Hubs, Sculpteo, i.materialise (shutting down March 2026), Treatstock. No dominant SMB bureau-OS; the category is **fragmented and underserved**.
competitive_landscape.incumbent_age_years: Most incumbents are 6–11 years old. No legacy 20-year player. This is both opportunity (no entrenched UI rot) and risk (incumbents are modern and well-funded, less obvious replatform wedge than e.g. JobBOSS).
competitive_landscape.user_satisfaction_signals: AMFG and industry analysts identify clear pain: '5 signs your 3D printing service bureau needs workflow software', spreadsheet-based quoting can take 'hours to a full business day', staff manually re-key data across CRM + accounting + spreadsheets, real-time order status not visible to customers, mistakes from typing wrong numbers / formulas. Reddit and r/3Dprinting threads frequently lament Excel-based pricing, dropped quote follow-ups, and lack of customer self-serve. DigiFabster reviews highlight high pricing as a barrier; MakerOS reviews note feature gaps. **The gap is workflow maturity, not dissatisfaction with a dominant incumbent.**
competitive_landscape.recent_funding_or_ma: Quiet category. Phasio raised seed funding (Singapore, ~2023, TechCrunch coverage). Xometry continues to grow (FY2025 USD 687m, +30% YoY) and is acquiring capabilities (e.g. Thomasnet earlier). i.materialise is winding down its consumer platform March 2026 — possible orphan customers. No major SMB bureau-OS raise reported in 2025–26. Less VC-frothy than finishing/fab.
competitive_landscape.ai_disruption_risk: High and rising. AutoQuote3D, Phasio, DigiFabster, and Xometry all pushing AI for geometry-based DFM, instant quoting, lead-time prediction. A generic 'AI quote tool' is already crowded. Differentiation has to come from workflow + Australia/NZ depth, not AI alone.

opportunity_quality.core_pain: **Quote-to-delivery workflow** is unsolved at the SMB end. Bureau receives STL/STEP via email → estimator opens in slicer (Bambu Studio / PrusaSlicer / nTopology) → guesses material+time+post-processing → quote in Excel → invoice via Xero → tracks across printers via whiteboard or Trello → ships → customer asks for cert/FAI which is manually compiled. Multiple disconnected tools: CAM/slicer + email + Trello + Xero + Stripe + WhatsApp. No customer portal for status. Instant-quote upload tools exist but are quoting-only; workflow + traceability + certification + accounting integration is still fragmented.
opportunity_quality.moat_source: Weaker than fab/finishing. (1) Workflow data accumulates but switching costs are lower (bureaus are smaller, more agile, less data-heavy). (2) Slicer/CAM integrations (Bambu, Prusa, PreForm, GrabCAD Print) help. (3) Embedded payments + customer portal stickiness. (4) ISO 13485 / AS9100 / FAA-Part 145 traceability for premium bureaus (aerospace, medical). (5) Australian regional network effects — local material suppliers, post/logistics. The honest answer: the moat is thinner than finishing because the category is younger and less data-intensive.
opportunity_quality.critical_integrations: Must-have: Xero, MYOB, Stripe, Cura/Bambu/Prusa STL upload, STEP/STL viewer, email/PDF, Stripe/Square. Important: AusPost / Sendle / Aramex shipping, slicer time/material estimates (parsed from G-code). Nice-to-have: GrabCAD Print, PreForm (Formlabs), nTopology, instant DFM AI, Materialise Magics.
opportunity_quality.incumbent_ehr_lock_in: Very low. Most bureaus on Excel + Xero/MYOB + Trello. Direct rip-and-replace is the dominant scenario.

build_difficulty.regulatory_complexity: Low for general 3D printing. Medical-grade (ISO 13485 + biocompatibility ISO 10993) and aerospace (AS9100 + AS9102 FAI) tiers are high-complexity but optional. Most bureaus stay in the general/industrial tier with light ISO 9001 only.
build_difficulty.regulatory_changes_2025_2026: (1) **TGA medical device reforms** — Australian TGA tightening custom-made medical device pathway through 2024–2026 (alignment with EU MDR-style requirements); 3D-printed medical/dental devices face increased documentation requirements. (2) **AASB S2 climate disclosures** — energy reporting per print job will matter for bureaus serving large customers from 2026. (3) **ISO/ASTM 52900-series** additive manufacturing standards continuing to mature. (4) **FAA / EASA additive certification** maturing (relevant for AU aerospace bureaus serving global supply chains). (5) **i.materialise winding down March 2026** — small but real customer orphan event creating switching demand. None are catastrophic forcing functions; medical TGA is the strongest pull.
build_difficulty.domain_depth: Moderate. Slicers, materials (PLA / PETG / nylon / resin / metal powder), print technologies (FDM / SLA / SLS / DMLS / MJF), post-processing, and DFM are learnable in 3–6 months by a technical founder. Manuva founder is already technically literate — easier than finishing.
build_difficulty.mvp_effort: 5–7 months for credible v1 (quote upload + STL viewer + workflow board + Xero invoice + customer status portal). 8–10 months to add multi-printer queue + DFM AI + ISO 13485 traceability.
build_difficulty.technical_risks: (1) STL/STEP/3MF parsing + bounding box + volume calc — straightforward (libraries: trimesh, OCCT, three.js). (2) AI DFM (printability, wall thickness, overhangs) — non-trivial but tractable; can leverage commodity models. (3) Slicer integration for accurate cost/time — depends on slicer (Cura/Bambu have APIs/G-code parsing). (4) Multi-printer queue + scheduling is the most non-trivial piece (real-time, multi-tenant). No truly hard ML.
build_difficulty.state_by_state_variance_au: Negligible. Federal product safety, TGA federal, GST federal. No state-by-state rule engine needed.
build_difficulty.data_residency_requirement: Optional. Defence and TGA-regulated work may want AU-hosted; Supabase Sydney covers. Not a blocker for general bureau work.

distribution_difficulty.channel_options: (1) **SEO / content** — bureau owners are heavy Googlers; long-tail keywords ('3D printing service bureau software AU', 'instant 3D print quoting Xero') are winnable. (2) **Reddit / r/3Dprinting / r/FormLabs / r/Sculpteo** — high-engagement community. (3) **Slicer integrations / app stores** — Bambu Studio plugins, GrabCAD partnerships. (4) **YouTube / influencers** — Maker's Muse (AU), Teaching Tech (AU), Joel Telling reach the audience. (5) **Trade shows** — Australian Manufacturing Week (additive zone), 3D Print Expo, Formnext (Frankfurt, global). (6) **AMTIL / AMHub** — Advanced Manufacturing Growth Centre (AMGC) has additive programs in AU. (7) **Cold outbound** — small but reachable target list (~150–300 bureaus AU). (8) **i.materialise sunset (Mar 2026)** — opportunity to capture orphaned customers.
distribution_difficulty.trade_association_count_au: 2–4: AMTIL (additive sub-group), AMGC (Advanced Manufacturing Growth Centre — funded by federal govt), Additive Manufacturing Hub (AMHub, VIC), Australian Manufacturing Growth Centre.
distribution_difficulty.trade_publication_count: ~3–6: AMT magazine (AMTIL), Manufacturers' Monthly, @AuManufacturing newsletter, 3D Printing Industry, All3DP, Voxelmatters, TCT Magazine (global but read in AU).
distribution_difficulty.industry_facebook_group_size: Moderate. AU-specific 3D printing groups (e.g. 'Australian 3D Printing', 'AU 3D Printing & Makers') aggregate ~20k–50k hobbyists + small bureaus. Reddit r/3Dprinting has ~2.5m members (global). Better community channel than fab/finishing.
distribution_difficulty.conference_event_count_au: 2–4 sub-$10k options: Australian Manufacturing Week (additive zone), AMHub events, 3D Print Sydney/Melbourne meetups, AMTIL state expos.
distribution_difficulty.cold_outbound_viability: High for the named bureaus (~150–300), low for the long tail of hobbyist-turned-bureaus (hard to identify systematically). Directory scraping (Voxelmatters, All3DP, Treatstock) yields a clean target list.
distribution_difficulty.founder_market_fit_proxy: Strong. Bureau owners are technical, software-friendly, and respond to peers who understand slicers and DFM. Less insider-gated than finishing or vet. Manuva founder is well-positioned culturally.
distribution_difficulty.case_study_acquisition_cost: Low-to-moderate. First 5 references probably 2–4 months: target ~30 bureaus via cold email + Reddit / community presence, 10–15 demos, 5 free pilots. Bureaus are accustomed to trying new tools.
distribution_difficulty.content_seo_competitiveness: Moderate. Generic '3D printing quoting software' dominated by DigiFabster / MakerOS / Phasio. AU-localised long tail is wide open. Topical: '3D printing service bureau Australia', 'instant quote STL upload Xero', 'AS9100 additive traceability'.
distribution_difficulty.insurer_or_gatekeeper_dependency: None for general work. Medical/aerospace bureaus depend on TGA / FAA / OEM approval flows; these are workflow inputs, not blocking APIs.

personal_fit.manuva_data_model_reuse_pct: ~40–55%. Direct reuse: tenants, RLS, users/roles, suppliers, items (materials), locations, invoicing, activity_log. New: STL/STEP file model, print jobs vs production orders, slicer parameter store, printer asset/queue model, customer self-serve portal, DFM analysis records. Smaller overlap than fab/finishing because production-order semantics differ more.
personal_fit.manuva_code_reuse: High. Next.js + Supabase + RLS + tenant context + design system + Xero/MYOB integration + invite/auth + activity_log all transfer cleanly. UI patterns reusable.
personal_fit.buyer_persona_overlap_with_manuva: Very low. 3D bureau owners are distinct from MTS product manufacturers. No meaningful cross-sell. Fresh GTM and brand required.
personal_fit.adjacency_to_manufacturing: Adjacent but a step further from Manuva's core than fab. Same manufacturing-ops vocabulary, very different workflow (digital-file-first, no BOM in the traditional sense, customer-uploaded geometry).
personal_fit.technical_moat_durability_months: 6–12 months. The category is the most replicable of the three — AI-coding-tool-equipped competitor could ship an MVP fast, and there are already 6–10 modern players. Moat must come from AU/NZ depth, integrations, payments, and community — not raw product.

unit_economics.gross_margin_sensitivity: Healthy but watch AI costs. Core SaaS workflow ~85% margin. STL viewer is client-side (three.js). DFM / AI quoting incurs ~AUD 0.05–0.30 per quote (geometry analysis); chargeable as upsell. No SMS/voice/human-in-loop in core. Storage costs slightly higher than typical SaaS due to STL/STEP files (~5–50MB each); manageable via S3-tier or per-tenant quota.
unit_economics.multi_location_natural: Low. Most bureaus are single-site. ~10–15% have 2 locations. Less multi-site upside than fab or finishing.
unit_economics.churn_risk: Moderate-to-high. Bureaus are smaller, more cash-constrained, more likely to churn during downturns. Many are 1–2 person operations vulnerable to founder burnout / pivot. Expected gross churn 10–15%/yr. Mitigated by embedded payments stickiness.
unit_economics.customers_needed_for_target_arr: At AUD 275/mo blended: ~305 paying customers for AUD 1m ARR. AU TAM only ~150–300 bureaus → cannot hit AUD 1m ARR on AU alone; must expand to NZ + UK + US from day 1, or layer marketplace / payments revenue. **This is the binding economic constraint for this vertical.**
